idea_stance.span: It's a decent idea — the problem is real (decision fatigue, food waste) and the photo-input angle solves the biggest friction point of meal-planning apps, which is tedious manual entry.
idea_stance.label: encouraging

names_flaws.span: But it's been tried many times, so the question isn't really "is the idea good" — it's "can you solve the problems that sank previous attempts?"
Fridge photos have occluded items, opaque containers, stuff in drawers.
If the app says "you have no eggs" and you do, trust erodes fast.
Pantry and freezer items matter for most recipes, and a fridge photo misses them.
A photo is a snapshot; by Wednesday it's wrong, and the meal plan and grocery list degrade.
Generic plans get abandoned within weeks.

verdict.span: It's a decent idea — the problem is real (decision fatigue, food waste) and the photo-input angle solves the biggest friction point of meal-planning apps, which is tedious manual entry.
verdict.label: conditional
